messages:
Connor O'Brien: Drafting release comms for the streaming/tool-calling/structured-output examples refresh. Posting here for final eyes before we hit publish + SDK releases. Target ship window: Thu (tomorrow) 10:00am PT docs publish, SDK releases rolling through by EOD.

Connor O'Brien: Proposed internal announcement (Slack + email blurb):

**DevEx update: refreshed streaming + tool calling + structured output examples are live**

We’ve updated Redwood’s developer-facing examples across Python/TypeScript/Go + docs to reflect the canonical patterns for:
- Streaming responses (consistent event handling + final message assembly)
- Tool calling (partial args handling, parallel calls, tool-result messages)
- Structured output (JSON schema constraints + validation/retry guidance)

What changed:
- Docs guides refreshed + new “Known pitfalls” section (partial tool args, stream disconnects, incremental JSON)
- Runnable examples added/updated in redwood-examples
- Quickstarts updated for agentic workflows template
- Golden transcript tests added to reduce regressions across SDKs

Links:
- Docs PRs (merged):
  - Streaming guide: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-docs/pull/512
  - Tool calling + pitfalls: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-docs/pull/519
  - Structured output + JSON schema: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-docs/pull/527
  - Code tab fix: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-docs/pull/534
- Examples (merged):
  - Streaming + tool calling samples: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-examples/pull/311
  - Structured output sample: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-examples/pull/318
- SDK PRs (merged):
  - Python examples refresh: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk-python/pull/2874
  - Python golden tests: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk-python/pull/2881
  - TS tool calling types + examples: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk-typescript/pull/1932
  - TS streaming loop refactor: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk-typescript/pull/1940
  - Go streaming loop update: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk-go/pull/744
  - Go tool calling sample: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk-go/pull/752

Rollout:
- Docs publish: Thu 10:00am PT
- Quickstarts publish: Thu ~11:00am PT (after docs indexing)
- SDK releases: Thu afternoon (exact versions in #eng-releases)

Ask:
- Support/SE: please route any streaming/tool-calling confusion to the new pitfalls section + runnable examples. Report anything still confusing to @Monica Patel / @Elliot Price.

Connor O'Brien: Specific question: does anyone want explicit callout language re: model variability for structured output (i.e., “schema-constrained best effort, validate + retry”) in the announcement itself, or keep it as docs-only?

Alex Martinez: +1 to keep announcement high level but include one sentence that sets expectations. Something like: “Structured output behavior can vary by model; examples show validation and safe fallbacks.”

Elliot Price: Agree. We already have that callout in the structured output guide intro + the support matrix section. But having a short sentence in the announcement will prevent overpromising.

Monica Patel: Looks good. One tweak: can we replace “event handling” with “event types + deltas + final assembly”? That’s what people were getting wrong in older snippets.

Ibrahim Khan: Also: please link the event conventions doc internally (Confluence) for folks writing new examples. Not for external comms, but for internal announcement it’s useful.

Connor O'Brien: Yep. Adding internal-only links under the main blurb. (Not going to the public changelog.)

Connor O'Brien: Adding:
- Event model conventions (internal): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ENGDX/Streaming+event+model+conventions
- Tool calling parity checklist (internal): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ENGDX/Tool+calling+parity+guidelines

Renee Sullivan: Suggestion for phrasing (external-friendly):
“Copy/paste examples now match the current SDK interfaces and include end-to-end handling for partial tool arguments + JSON validation.”

Wei Chen: Minor: in the docs publish timing, note that site may take ~15-30 min for cache + search indexing. Otherwise people will think links are broken.

Nikhil Sharma: Re: structured output expectations — yes, add the one-liner. Also avoid “guarantees” language. We’ve been using “schema-constrained output” / “validated structured output” consistently.

Dev Patel: Support request: include the “Known pitfalls” link explicitly (whatever the final docs URL is) and mention the top two pain points:
1) tool args can be partial across chunks
2) JSON can be invalid until final chunk
That’ll reduce “this is broken” pings.

Markus Klein: +1. Also add “parallel tool calls are supported but results must be sent back as tool-result messages” (lots of customer confusion there).

Sahana Iyer: Golden tests note is good. If you want to be extra clear: “golden transcript fixtures” (people ask what golden means).

Jean-Paul Laurent: Quickstarts timing works. I’ll confirm smoke tests are green before 11am PT. If anything slips, I’ll post in thread + #devex.

Connor O'Brien: Updates incorporated. Revised draft:

**DevEx update: refreshed streaming + tool calling + structured output examples are live**

We’ve updated Redwood’s developer-facing examples across Python/TypeScript/Go + docs to reflect the canonical patterns for:
- Streaming responses (event types, deltas, final assembly, error handling)
- Tool calling (partial args handling, parallel calls, tool-result messages)
- Structured output (JSON schema constraints + validation/retry guidance)

Note: structured output behavior can vary by model. The guides/examples show how to validate, handle failures safely, and retry when needed.

New/updated resources:
- Docs guides (public):
  - Streaming guide: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-docs/pull/512
  - Tool calling + Known pitfalls: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-docs/pull/519
  - Structured output + JSON schema + validation: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-docs/pull/527
- Runnable examples (public):
  - Streaming + tool calling: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-examples/pull/311
  - Structured output sample: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-examples/pull/318
- SDK updates (public):
  - Python: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk-python/pull/2874 (examples), https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk-python/pull/2881 (golden transcript fixtures)
  - TypeScript: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk-typescript/pull/1932, https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk-typescript/pull/1940
  - Go: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk-go/pull/744, https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk-go/pull/752

Rollout:
- Docs publish: Thu 10:00am PT (allow 15–30 min for cache/search indexing)
- Quickstarts publish: Thu ~11:00am PT
- SDK releases: Thu afternoon (versions + changelog in #eng-releases)

Support/SE: If customers hit issues, please start with the “Known pitfalls” section and runnable samples. If anything remains confusing or broken, flag @Monica Patel / @Elliot Price with repro.

Internal reference (for anyone writing future snippets):
- Event model conventions: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ENGDX/Streaming+event+model+conventions
- Tool calling parity checklist: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ENGDX/Tool+calling+parity+guidelines

Connor O'Brien: Any last nits? If no objections by 4pm PT, I’ll schedule the announcement + coordinate with #eng-releases.

Alex Martinez: LGTM. :thumbsup:

Elliot Price: Good from docs. :white_check_mark:

Monica Patel: Good from SDKs. :shipit:

Dev Patel: Please tag #support in the actual announcement so it gets seen. Otherwise 👍

Connor O'Brien: Will do. Scheduling now.
